title: In mice, a population of male germ cells show characteristics of nonapoptotic cell death during G0 arrest.
abstract: In mammals, a small population of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is established shortly after birth. These cells self-renew and produce sperm for the male's reproductive lifespan, passing the genome on to the next generation. Establishment of a population of SSCs with high genomic integrity is essential. SSCs are derived from a much larger precursor population of male germ cells (MGCs) that differentiate during fetal life. During the last third of gestation, MGCs undergo a prolonged period of G0 cell cycle arrest during which they sustain high levels of transcription and acquire epigenetic programming for SSC fate. Although these differentiation steps can cause cellular and genomic damage, it has been unclear whether selection for germ cell quality occurs during G0 arrest since no classic markers of cell death have been detected. In this study, we used a mouse model to characterize a population of MGCs that begin to accumulate markers of cell death, such as AnnexinV (AnV) and propidium iodide (PI), at E16.5. The AnV- and PI-positive MGC population is characterized by low expression of the RNA-binding protein, Dead End 1, and exhibits dsDNA breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction. Interestingly, we do not see evidence of an active cell death cascade until the time of birth, when phosphorylation of MLKL, a hallmark of necroptotic cell death, occurs. Based on these findings, we propose that variable cellular health is an important basis for selection of SSC precursors.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: Syncrip coordinates with hnRNPK to regulate PPV NS1 mRNA splicing and facilitate viral replication.
abstract: Porcine parvovirus (PPV) relies on alternative splicing of the nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) transcript to generate nonstructural protein 2 (NS2), but the host factors coordinating this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we identified heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K (hnRNPK) as a regulator of PPV NS1-to-NS2 mRNA splicing in PK-15 cells. hnRNPK specifically associated with NS1 mRNA, and PPV infection increased hnRNPK expression in a time- and multiplicity-of-infection-dependent manner. hnRNPK overexpression decreased the NS1/NS2 mRNA and protein ratios and increased viral DNA accumulation, whereas hnRNPK knockout produced the opposite effects. hnRNPK and the previously identified splicing regulator synaptotagmin-binding, cytoplasmic RNA-interacting protein (Syncrip) additively promoted NS1-to-NS2 splicing and PPV replication. Double-knockout and reconstitution experiments further showed that co-expression of hnRNPK and Syncrip restored NS2 production and viral replication more effectively than either factor alone. Domain-mapping analyses identified the K-protein interaction region (KI) of hnRNPK and the RNA recognition motif 2 (RRM2) region of Syncrip as the principal regions supporting this activity. hnRNPK associated directly with Syncrip, and Syncrip was required for efficient recruitment of hnRNPK to NS1 mRNA. In addition, hnRNPK associated with serine- and arginine-rich splicing factor 1 (SRSF1) in an RNA-independent manner during PPV infection. These findings support a model in which a Syncrip-hnRNPK complex promotes PPV NS1-to-NS2 alternative splicing and thereby facilitates viral replication, while identifying SRSF1 as a candidate component of the associated host splicing machinery.IMPORTANCEPorcine parvovirus (PPV) causes reproductive failure in swine and relies extensively on host RNA-processing machinery because of its limited coding capacity. Alternative splicing of the PPV nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) transcript generates nonstructural protein 2 (NS2), but the host factors controlling this process remain poorly defined. Here, we identify heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K (hnRNPK) as a host regulator of PPV mRNA splicing and replication. hnRNPK acts additively with synaptotagmin-binding, cytoplasmic RNA-interacting protein (Syncrip) to promote NS1-to-NS2 mRNA splicing, increase NS2 production, and support viral DNA replication. Syncrip facilitates the association of hnRNPK with NS1 mRNA, and defined regions within both proteins contribute to this activity. hnRNPK also associates with the cellular splicing factor serine- and arginine-rich splicing factor 1 (SRSF1) during PPV infection. These findings reveal a host RNA-binding protein network that PPV exploits to expand its coding capacity and promote replication.

title: Hepatic Lipid Stress Drives Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis Progression through FTO O-GlcNAcylation-Induced m6A Demethylation of HRAS.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by nutrient stress through incompletely defined epigenetic mechanisms. This study demonstrates that lipid stress activates the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP), elevating O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) at Ser195. This post-translational modification recruits the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 20 (USP20), displaces the E3 ligase F-box and WD repeat domain containing 7 (FBXW7), and enhances FTO protein stability and m6A demethylase activity. O-GlcNAc-dependent FTO activation removes m6A from Harvey rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (HRAS) mRNA, evades YTH N6‑methyladenosine RNA binding protein 2 (YTHDF2)‑mediated degradation, and prolongs transcript half-life. Subsequent HRAS upregulation activates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, driving hepatic steatosis and inflammation. Administration of a novel cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) designed to block FTO O-GlcNAcylation at Ser195 effectively ameliorates MASH progression in vitro and in vivo. These findings establish FTO O-GlcNAcylation as a druggable metabolic-epigenetic checkpoint in MASH pathogenesis, revealing a promising therapeutic strategy for this increasingly prevalent liver disease.

title: Using Solution NMR to Study the RNA-Binding Properties and Molecular Mechanisms of the RNA Helicase DDX3X.
abstract: DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) are a family of enzymes that participate in nearly all aspects of cellular RNA metabolism by remodeling RNA structures. Among them, DDX3X plays key roles in diverse physiological processes, including the translational regulation of gene expression, and its malfunction is frequently associated with the onset of disease. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms of DDX3X, solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insights into its RNA-binding properties, dynamic behavior, and intermolecular interactions, complementing conventional structural approaches aimed at determining high-resolution atomic models. In this chapter, we present a detailed protocol for preparing isotopically labeled proteins for NMR analysis, using the minimal functional core region of DDX3X as an example. The presented protocol enables the production of large amounts of purified protein, which can also be adapted for other in vitro structural and biochemical experiments used to characterize helicase function.

title: Mapping of RNA Helicase Dynamics by HDX-MS.
abstract: RNA helicases are RNA-binding enzymes that remodel RNA structures and ribonucleoprotein complexes through regulated conformational changes. Their RecA-like catalytic cores cooperate with auxiliary domains, many of which contain flexible or partially disordered regions whose rearrangements are difficult to characterize using static structural methods. Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) overcomes this limitation by examining protein conformation in solution, providing peptide-resolved information on local stability, dynamics, and ligand-dependent structural changes. In this chapter, we describe a bottom-up HDX-MS workflow for mapping RNA helicase-RNA interactions and conformational dynamics, using the Pseudomonas aeruginosa DExH-box helicase HrpB as a model. The protocol covers sample preparation, deuterium labeling, quenching, protein digestion, peptide separation, MS acquisition, and data analysis. We outline practical guidelines for optimizing peptide coverage, preserving deuterium labeling throughout the workflow, and obtaining quantitative comparisons between the apo and RNA-bound states. The chapter provides a framework for using HDX-MS to identify where RNA, nucleotides, and small-molecule inhibitors bind, to characterize the conformational changes they induce, and to connect these dynamics to the RNA helicase mechanism of action.

title: Key Points to Consider When Studying RNA Remodeling by Proteins.
abstract: Cellular RNAs depend on proteins for efficient folding to specific functional structures and for transitions between functional structures. This dependence arises from intrinsic properties of RNA structure. Specifically, RNAs possess stable local structure, largely in the form of helices, and there are abundant opportunities for RNAs to form alternative helices and tertiary contacts and therefore to populate alternative structures. Proteins with RNA chaperone activity, either ATP-dependent or ATP-independent, can promote structural transitions by interacting with single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) to compete away partner interactions and then release ssRNA so that it can form new interactions. In this chapter, we review the basic properties of RNA and the proteins that function as chaperones and remodelers. We then use these properties as a foundation to explore key points for the design and interpretation of experiments that probe RNA rearrangements and their acceleration by proteins.

title: smiMAD: Adaptive multi-view graph learning for paired spatial omics integration.
abstract: Paired spatial omics technologies measure transcriptomic profiles together with epigenomic or proteomic profiles while preserving tissue context. Integration remains challenging because modalities differ in feature distributions, sparsity, and spatial dependencies. Existing methods may not fully model complementary graph views or adapt spatial constraints, limiting preservation of spatial organization and modality-specific information. We present smiMAD for paired spatial omics integration. smiMAD models spatial-neighborhood and molecular-feature graphs through graph-view-specific and common-information branches. An adaptive gate integrates graph-view and modality information, while an alignment-decorrelation objective promotes common-information embedding consistency and reduces branch redundancy. A dynamic spatial-consistency strategy progressively relaxes spatial constraints during training. Across 17 simulated and 15 real RNA-ATAC and RNA-protein datasets, smiMAD achieved competitive clustering accuracy, spatial coherence, and multimodal integration performance. Molecular marker patterns provided support for the inferred spatial regions. The source code is available at https://github.com/fdu-wangfeilab/smiMAD, with the version used in this study archived at https://zenodo.org/records/22931624. Data are available at https://zenodo.org/records/17207079.

title: Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery.
abstract: A key pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is transactive response DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43, encoded by TARDBP) proteinopathy. Mutations in TARDBP and cellular stress can drive nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43. TDP-43 is an essential nuclear RNA-binding protein that regulates RNA metabolism, and cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation leads to aberrant splicing of essential neuronal transcripts including stathmin-2 (STMN2) and unc-13 homolog A (UNC13A). Dysregulated RNA splicing causes cryptic exon (CE) inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A mRNA, resulting in non-functional proteins and disruption of axonal regeneration and synaptic integrity. Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides and gene-editing platforms can correct STMN2 and UNC13A mis-splicing defects. However, restoring STMN2 and UNC13A expression alone is not sufficient to regenerate neuromuscular junctions or reverse skeletal muscle atrophy, both of which are crucial for functional recovery in patients with ALS. We reviewed gene-targeted treatment strategies and rehabilitative mechanisms that inhibit ALS progression and reverse neuromuscular degeneration by analyzing databases, including Google Scholar, PubMed, and ScienceDirect. We proposed a dual-modality therapeutic approach integrating base-editing-mediated gene therapy with exercise-based rehabilitation. Antisense oligonucleotides and genome editing can restore transcript fidelity by preventing cryptic exons inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A, thereby stabilizing neuronal function. Gene-targeted therapies halt ALS progression; however, these treatments alone are insufficient to reverse neuromuscular degeneration or achieve functional recovery needed for patients with ALS to return to daily life. Integrated rehabilitation is a crucial step in gene-targeted therapy for ALS. This strategy halts disease progression and restores neuromuscular function, thereby improving the lifespan and quality of life of patients with ALS.

title: Probing the Role of RNA Helicases in Modulating Stress Granules, RNA Localization, and P-Body Docking.
abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are cytoplasmic, membrane-less ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules that form in response to cellular stress following the inhibition of translation initiation. Their assembly, composition, and crosstalk with processing bodies (P-bodies) are mediated by protein-protein, RNA-protein, and RNA-RNA interactions. DEAD/DEAH-box RNA helicases are key regulators of stress granules. Here, we present standardized protocols for (i) immunofluorescence of stress granule and P-body scaffold proteins and helicases, (ii) single-molecule RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (smRNA FISH), and (iii) quantitative image analysis using Imaris software, including single-cell and nuclear segmentation, stress granule and P-body surface rendering, docking interaction analysis, and RNA spot detection.

title: RBMS1 Contributes to Early Arteriovenous Fistula Neointimal Remodeling Through Modulation of VSMC Phenotypic Responses.
abstract: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation initiates stage-dependent remodeling of the venous outflow tract. Neointimal hyperplasia is a common component of this response, but its post-transcriptional regulation remains unclear. Here, analyses of human AVF datasets and tissue specimens characterized RNA-binding motif single-stranded interacting protein 1 (RBMS1) expression in postoperative AVFs, whereas a day-14 mouse AVF model and cultured vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) were used to investigate its role in early neointimal remodeling. Smooth muscle-targeted RBMS1 overexpression aggravated neointimal formation, whereas conditional RBMS1 deletion attenuated it in murine AVFs. In cultured VSMCs, RBMS1 overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and the transition from contractile to synthetic marker expression, whereas RBMS1 silencing produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, RBMS1 bound myelin protein zero-like 1 (MPZL1) mRNA and promoted exon 5 skipping, generating the MPZL1-Δ5 isoform. MPZL1-Δ5 overexpression reproduced selected RBMS1-associated VSMC responses and increased neointimal hyperplasia in vivo, including in RBMS1-deficient mice. MPZL1-Δ5 further interacted with GTPase-activating protein SH3 domain-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) and enhanced protein kinase B (AKT) activation, whereas G3BP1 silencing attenuated RBMS1- or MPZL1-Δ5-induced VSMC responses. Together, these findings identify the RBMS1-MPZL1-Δ5-G3BP1-AKT pathway as an important VSMC-associated mechanism contributing to neointimal remodeling during the early postoperative phase of experimental AVFs.

title: Zika virus produces two isoforms of the NS2A protein that play mutually exclusive roles in viral replication and virion assembly.
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV), dengue virus, and several other orthoflaviviruses cause disease outbreaks in human and animal populations worldwide. The orthoflaviviral nonstructural protein 2A (NS2A) is critical for both viral replication and virion assembly. However, due to its small size, hydrophobicity, and the absence of structural information or protein-specific antibodies, we lack a clear understanding of how NS2A participates in these disparate processes. Here, using endogenously tagged NS2A-containing viral RNAs, we reveal that two NS2A isoforms are present during ZIKV infection, including both full-length NS2A and a C-terminally truncated isoform, termed NS2Aα. Phylogenetic and conservation analyses combined with polyprotein cleavage assays suggest that both NS2A isoforms are generated via the viral protease and are conserved across the Orthoflavivirus genus. Finally, using assays for viral replication and infectious particle production, we demonstrate that the two distinct NS2A isoforms function at different stages of the viral life cycle, with full-length NS2A required for viral RNA replication and NS2Aα important for virion assembly. Taken together, our data helps shed light on the form(s) and function(s) of the NS2A protein and suggests that each NS2A isoform plays a mutually exclusive role in the orthoflaviviral life cycle.

title: Assays to Study SUMOylation of RNA Helicase DHX9.
abstract: RNA helicase DHX9 is a multi-functional protein governing transcriptional modulation, RNA processing, R-loop balance, and genome stability. SUMOylation is a post-translational modification that adds a critical regulatory layer to protein function by diversifying subcellular localization, stability, enzymatic activity, and protein-protein interactions. This protocol describes a basic but detailed approach for the analysis of DHX9 SUMOylation. We demonstrate that accurate site identification, specifically at Lysine 120 (K120), is the prerequisite for defining the molecular mechanism of this modification. Identifying the K120 acceptor site enables the generation of specific mutants to dissect how DHX9 SUMOylation orchestrates the protein interactions necessary to preserve genomic integrity. Furthermore, this protocol provides a versatile framework for characterizing the SUMOylation of other RNA helicases involved in RNA regulation.

title: Fast Analysis of RNA from Transcription and Rho-Dependent Termination Assays Using Automated Capillary Electrophoresis.
abstract: Conventional analysis of RNA products synthesized by bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP) in in vitro transcription assays relies on radioactive labeling, followed by separation of labeled RNAs by denaturing urea-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE). This approach provides excellent resolution across a wide range of RNA lengths (from 2 nt to several hundred nucleotides), but the use of radioisotopes requires specialized facilities, strict waste-disposal procedures, and is often restricted. To circumvent these limitations, we adapted a standard in vitro transcription assay for use with the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer capillary electrophoresis system. Here, we describe the application of this method to analyze run-off transcription by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) RNAP and its transcription termination products generated by the Mtb Rho factor. We demonstrate that RNAs produced in in vitro transcription reactions can be detected and quantified without radioactive labeling, simplifying and accelerating the workflow. Although capillary electrophoresis lacks the single-nucleotide resolution of denaturing urea-PAGE, it provides a practical alternative that is compatible with any laboratory environment. This protocol is broadly applicable for analyzing RNA products generated by in vitro transcription with any bacterial RNAP, in the presence or absence of RNA remodeling factors such as the Rho protein.

title: Purification of C/D-Box snoRNP and Fibrillarin-Associated Factors from Arabidopsis thaliana Plants Using GFP-Tagged Proteins.
abstract: Fibrillarin is an evolutionarily conserved methyltransferase found in Archaea, algae, yeast, animals, and plants. It catalyzes the 2'-O-methylation (2'-O-Me) of ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs), small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs), small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs), and transfer RNAs (tRNAs) as well as the glutamine methylation (Qme) in histone H2A. Fibrillarin interacts with specific accessory proteins and snoRNA guides to perform 2'-O-Me, although it can also act independently in the case of Qme. Additionally, fibrillarin has been reported to exhibit ribonuclease activity and interact with long non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression. To identify proteins and RNAs that interact with fibrillarin in vivo, we developed a protocol-detailed herein-combining the immunoprecipitation (IP) of a fibrillarin-Yellow Fluorescent Protein (FIB2-YFP) fusion protein in Arabidopsis thaliana with high-sensitivity liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis.

title: PRRSV infection induces mitochondrial damage and releases mitochondrial dsRNA to activate the NLRP3-dependent inflammatory response.
abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), caused by the PRRS virus (PRRSV), remains one of the most economically significant infectious diseases affecting the global swine industry, resulting in annual losses exceeding US $1.2 billion in the USA alone. PRRSV infects porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs) and induces profound mitochondrial dysfunction, leading to the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). However, the mechanisms by which PRRSV-induced mitochondrial damage acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) to trigger inflammatory responses have not been fully elucidated. Here, we report that highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) infection upregulates interleukin-1β (IL-1β) messenger RNA (mRNA) expression and protein secretion in a dose- and time-dependent manner. Transmission electron microscopy revealed progressive mitochondrial swelling, cristae disorganization, and matrix loss during HP-PRRSV infection. Using RNAscope combined with MitoGreen staining, we discovered that mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA), generated from bidirectional transcription of mitochondrial DNA, is released into the cytosol during PRRSV infection. In vitro, transcription-driven mtdsRNA or mtdsRNA isolated from PAMs directly activated the NLRP3 inflammasome, inducing caspase-1 cleavage and IL-1β secretion. Mechanistically, the PRRSV-encoded nonstructural protein 11 (nsp11) inhibited NLRP3-dependent inflammatory responses by suppressing the oligomerization of the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase recruitment domain (CARD) (ASC), thereby constraining excessive inflammation and establishing a delicate balance between pro-inflammatory signaling and viral immune evasion. Collectively, our findings identify mtdsRNA as a previously unrecognized mitochondrial DAMP that links PRRSV-induced mitochondrial injury to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, while also revealing a counter-regulatory role for nsp11 in modulating inflammation.

title: Myotube-derived exosomal miR-21 regulates the proliferation and adipogenic differentiation of ovine subcutaneous preadipocytes.
abstract: Skeletal muscle-derived signals contribute to intercellular communication with adipose tissue and may influence adipose tissue development; however, the role of exosomes in muscle-adipose crosstalk in sheep remains unclear. This study investigated whether myotube-derived exosomes regulate ovine preadipocyte proliferation and adipogenic differentiation through microRNA-mediated mechanisms. Myotube-preadipocyte interactions were examined using transwell co-culture, exosome isolation and characterization, small RNA sequencing, gain and loss function assays, dual-luciferase assays, and rescue experiments. Myotube co-culture promoted preadipocyte proliferation and suppressed adipogenic differentiation, as indicated by an increased proportion of 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) positive cells and proliferation related markers (P < 0.05) and reduced lipid accumulation and adipogenic markers (P < 0.05). Myotube-derived exosomes, which had a mean diameter of approximately 105 nm and expressed cluster of differentiation 9 (CD9), cluster of differentiation 63 (CD63), and tumor susceptibility gene 101 (TSG101), were internalized by preadipocytes and reproduced these effects (P < 0.05). Small RNA sequencing identified microRNA-21 (miR-21) as the most abundant exosomal miRNA, accounting for approximately 20% of miRNA-mapped reads. Overexpression of miR-21 promoted preadipocyte proliferation and suppressed adipogenic differentiation, whereas miR-21 inhibition produced the opposite responses (P < 0.05). Dual-luciferase assays confirmed programmed cell death protein 4 (PDCD4) and nuclear factor I A (NFIA) as direct targets of miR-21. Rescue experiments showed that PDCD4 and NFIA overexpression attenuated the proliferative and anti-adipogenic effects of miR-21, respectively. Collectively, myotube-derived exosomal miR-21 promotes ovine preadipocyte proliferation by regulating PDCD4 and suppresses adipogenic differentiation through NFIA. These findings reveal an exosome-mediated mechanism underlying muscle-adipose crosstalk in sheep.

title: Cell painting-based high-throughput assay for whole wastewater toxicity testing.
abstract: Microalgae are well-established model organisms for whole wastewater toxicity (WWT) assessment owing to their ease of cultivation and high sensitivity. However, the inherently low throughput and labor-intensive workflows of conventional microalga-based bioassays, such as ISO 8692:2012, prevent their application in large-scale WWT monitoring. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a scalable, high-throughput assay that integrates cell painting-based morphological profiling and supervised machine learning, which is validated using 25 individual chemicals, their mixture, and 578 real wastewater samples. By characterizing features associated with DNA, RNA, chloroplasts, the endoplasmic reticulum, the F-actin cytoskeleton, Golgi apparatus, and plasma membrane, cell painting provided a multidimensional phenotypic basis for model development. Compared to the ISO 8692:2012 standard, the proposed assay increases testing throughput by ∼21.7-fold and reduces testing time by ∼67.5%, enabling a comprehensive assessment of 100 wastewater treatment plants across China. Notably, greater treatment-process complexity was not consistently associated with higher WWT removal efficiency, challenging the prevailing practice of improving effluent risk control through additional treatment units. The proposed high-throughput assay offers a practical framework for WWT testing and large-scale water quality risk assessments.

title: Genetic background modulates MafAS64F-mediated islet ageing in male mice.
abstract: In monogenic diabetes, there is increasing recognition that common polygenic factors can modulate diabetes penetrance beyond the causative mutation(s). A naturally occurring mutation in the gene encoding the essential islet-enriched transcription factor MafA (MafAS64F) produces an unusually long-lived variant protein that predisposes male carriers to MODY. Here we investigated how genetic background modulates disease penetrance in MafaS64F/+ male mice. MafaS64F/+ male mice, either on a mixed genetic background (C57BL/6J and SJL/J) or backcrossed to a C57BL/6J background, were assessed for glucose levels, beta cell function and gene signatures associated with cellular ageing. RNA-seq analysis was performed to identify unique differentially expressed genes (DEGS) and pathways in mixed-background or C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets. These were overlaid on MafA CUT&RUN peaks to identify direct targets that could differentially impact beta cell function in each background. MafaS64F/+ male mice on a mixed background manifested overt diabetes, impaired insulin secretion, accelerated beta cell senescence and dysregulated circadian gene expression, while backcross to C57BL/6J prevented dysglycaemia and maintained insulin secretion in MafaS64F/+ male mice, comparable with control littermates. RNA-seq of C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mouse islets revealed relative normalisation of DEGs associated with cellular ageing and circadian regulation. In addition, islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice showed unique downregulation of retinoic acid signalling and cell cycle inhibitor p21, the latter of which modulates cellular ageing and diabetes seen in the mixed-background mouse islets. CUT&RUN mapping revealed that MafA directly impacted expression of (at least) retinoic acid receptor-α (encoded by Rara) in islets from C57BL/6J MafaS64F/+ male mice and circadian regulation in islets from mixed-background mice. In sum, these data show that genetic modifiers can impact beta cell regulation of retinoic acid signalling and circadian entrainment to modulate beta cell ageing and disease penetrance in mice modelling MAFA-MODY. Sequencing data were deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (accession no. GSE299343 for bulk RNA-seq and GSE298664 for CUT&RUN analyses).

title: Usp3 negatively regulates Mda5-mediated antiviral response by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination in black carp.
abstract: Melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) is a critical cytosolic RNA sensor that initiates type I interferon (IFN) signaling upon viral infection, and its activity must be tightly regulated to maintain immune homeostasis. Ubiquitin-specific protease 3 (USP3) has been identified as a negative regulator of RLR-mediated IFN signaling in mammals, yet its role in teleost antiviral immunity remains unknown. In this study, we cloned and characterized usp3 (bcusp3) from black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus). The full-length coding sequence of bcusp3 encodes a protein of 524 amino acids containing conserved ZnF-UBP and UCH domains. Overexpression of bcUsp3 significantly suppressed bcMda5-induced ifn promoter activation in a dose-dependent manner, whereas knockdown of bcUsp3 in MPF cells markedly enhanced ifn and interferon-stimulated gene (isg) expression and inhibited SVCV replication. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays revealed that bcUsp3 directly interacts with bcMda5. Furthermore, bcUsp3 over-expression reduced both total and K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5, indicating that bcUsp3 attenuates the K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that bcUsp3 functions as a negative regulator of bcMda5-mediated Ifn signaling by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination, providing the first evidence for the regulatory role of Usp3 in teleost antiviral innate immunity.

title: Relationship between neonatal glutamine supplementation and amino acid profiles, protein synthesis in splanchnic tissues and the plasma metabolome in 5-day-old piglets with low birth weight.
abstract: The incidence of low birthweight (LBiW) piglets, which show impaired growth compared to normal birthweight (NBiW) littermates, has increased with litter size. We previously reported that glutamine increased the bodyweight and plasma glutamine concentrations in LBiW piglets, with no effect on jejunal glutamine concentrations or glutamine transport and metabolism mRNA abundance. In this study, we investigated the effect of glutamine supplementation on proteinogenic free amino acid (FAA), protein-bound AA (PBAA) and AA-metabolite profiles, mRNA abundance, fractional protein synthesis (FPSR) and the plasma metabolome. At birth (0 days of age (d)), 24 pairs of male LBiW (1.10 kg ± 0.02) and NBiW (1.50 kg ± 0.02) littermates were selected. At 1 d, litters were standardized to 12 piglets, and piglets supplemented daily with either glutamine (1 g/kg bodyweight) or isonitrogenous amounts of alanine (1.22 g/kg bodyweight), until 5 d. Stomach content FAA, AA-metabolites, duodenal and liver tissue FAA, PBAA, AA-metabolites, biochemical indices, duodenal, colon and liver tissue FPSR, liver tissue and duodenal mucosa glutamine transport and metabolism mRNA abundance and the plasma metabolome were analysed. Stomach digesta glutamine (P < 0.001) and glutamate (LBiW, P = 0.02; NBiW, P = 0.03) concentrations were higher in glutamine than alanine piglets. Analysis by Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker Discovery using Latent Variable Approaches for Omics Studies showed glutamine, carnosine, citrulline and alanine separated the supplementation groups, whilst glutathione reductase, glutathione synthetase and tight junction protein 1 mRNA separated glutamine LBiW piglets from alanine. Duodenal RNA was lower and Protein-to-RNA ratio higher (P = 0.004) in glutamine than alanine LBiW piglets (P = 0.02). Colon FPSR was higher in NBiW than LBiW piglets supplemented with Ala. No effects on the plasma metabolome were observed. These results show that not all glutamine passed through the stomach, and that glutamine is absorbed and metabolised in the duodenum, potentially altering the intracellular pH, and appears to increase oxidative stress markers in the duodenum of LBiW piglets.

title: SREBF1 expression is associated with lipid metabolism-related signatures, and transient SREBF1 silencing is accompanied by increased apoptosis in pancreatic cancer cells.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal malignancy characterized by extensive metabolic adaptation. Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBF1) encodes sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), a transcriptional regulator of lipogenic genes. This study investigated the association between SREBF1 expression and lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features in PDAC and assessed cellular responses to transient SREBF1 silencing. SREBF1 expression was evaluated using RNA-sequencing data from TCGA-PAAD and GTEx and paired microarray data from GSE62452 and GSE183795. The analysis included 179 TCGA-PAAD tumors and 171 TCGA/GTEx non-tumor pancreatic samples, together with 61 matched tumor-adjacent pairs from GSE62452 and 102 matched pairs from GSE183795. TCGA-PAAD tumors were stratified at the median SREBF1 expression level for differential-expression analysis, GSEA, and GSVA. SREBF1 expression was higher in the TCGA/GTEx tumor-versus-normal comparison (P < 0.0001), with concordant increases in GSE62452 (P < 0.05) and GSE183795 (P < 0.01). SREBF1-high tumors exhibited lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features, including higher fatty-acid-metabolism and cholesterol-homeostasis pathway scores. In BxPC-3 and SW1990 cells, transient SREBF1 silencing with one selected siRNA was accompanied by decreased precursor SREBP1 (~ 122 kDa) and FASN protein levels, qualitatively reduced clonogenic outgrowth, and an increased Annexin V-positive apoptotic fraction. SREBF1 expression is associated with lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features in PDAC. Transient SREBF1 silencing was accompanied by reduced FASN protein levels, qualitatively reduced clonogenic outgrowth, and increased apoptosis. These findings identify SREBP1-associated lipid metabolism as a candidate vulnerability that requires further validation but do not establish a direct SREBP1-FASN-cell-survival mechanism or therapeutic efficacy.

title: Differential alternative splicing in skeletal muscle after 14 days immobilization-induced atrophy in young men.
abstract: Skeletal muscle disuse during injury decreases muscle mass and function. Previous studies have determined differential gene expression associated with atrophy, but changes in alternative splicing (AS) in response to unloading is poorly defined. This study aimed to identify global changes in differential alternative splicing (DAS) in skeletal muscle following unloading. Twenty-one healthy males (26.0 ± 5.7 years; 81.2 ± 11.6 kg) underwent 14 days unilateral knee-brace immobilization. Participants underwent strength and muscle mass assessment before and after the immobilization and vastus lateralis muscle biopsies were taken pre-immobilization, and on days 3 and 14. RNA-sequencing was performed, and DAS events were identified using the rMATS package. Leg strength decreased - 21.5 kg (P < 0.0001) while mid-thigh circumference was reduced ~ 2% (P = 0.016). A total of 157,464 and 159,395 splicing events affecting 15,219 and 15,374 genes identified on day 3 and 14, respectively. Most DAS events occurred in coding sequence regions and were primarily due to exon skipping. A higher number of DAS events were observed by day 14 than day 3, indicating time-dependent regulation. Gene Ontology analysis of DAS at day 14 revealed 37 enriched GO biological processes related to MAPK signalling, mitochondrial function, and organelle organization. Unloading-induced atrophy was associated with widespread changes in AS, particularly in genes linked to muscle maintenance and protein synthesis. AS appears to promote down-regulation of target genes and subsequent differentially enriched biological pathways associated with the functional outcomes of decreased muscle mass and strength. These findings indicate changes in alternative splicing is a regulatory mechanism in muscle wasting during immobilization.

title: Prenatal Cannabinoid Exposure Induces Sex-Specific Alterations in Fetal Growth and Placental Lipid Metabolism Gene Expression.
abstract: Prenatal cannabis use is becoming increasingly more commonplace. However, cannabis exposure is linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. The aim of this study was to determine the morphological and molecular effects of prenatal cannabinoid exposure on the placenta. Pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed daily to vaporized THC (100 mg/mL) starting at gestational day (GD)5 until GD19, when dams were sacrificed and fetuses and placentas collected. Fetuses were genotyped for genetic sex, and transcriptomic analysis was performed on male and female THC-exposed and control placentas. On GD19, only the female fetuses from the THC group were significantly larger than those of the control, with no significant differences in placental weights or fetal:placental weight ratios. RNA sequencing revealed enriched biological processes related to nutrient transport and lipid catabolism, protein-lipid complex formation, and lipoprotein particle remodeling and organization. Further transcriptomic analysis determined that the differentially expressed genes and enriched biological processes related to lipid metabolism were preferentially enriched in the female THC placentas compared to the male, suggesting a sex-specific effect. Collectively, these data present sex-specific effects of prenatal cannabinoid exposure on placental growth and global gene expression. These data also suggest that sex influences gene expression of genes related to lipid metabolism in the THC-exposed placentas.

title: Micro/Nanostructured Materials and Microfluidic Diagnostic Platforms Enable Multimodal Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), as pivotal targets in liquid biopsy, offer dynamic, multidimensional insights into tumor heterogeneity and metastatic progression. However, their extreme rarity, pronounced heterogeneity, and the complexity of the blood microenvironment severely constrain detection accuracy. Advances in micro/nanomaterials and functional device engineering have enabled substantial improvements in CTC enrichment efficiency by refining the topographical and chemical properties of capture interfaces. These innovations also provide a compatible foundation for multimodal molecular profiling. This review systematically outlines the structure-function relationships of functionalized nanomaterials, microfiltration substrates, and biomimetic microfluidic devices, highlighting how material parameters-such as nanoscale architectures and membrane pore sizes-govern CTC capture performance. We further explore the integration of micro/nanomaterials with functional platforms for multidimensional molecular analyses across DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Coupled with emerging digital PCR technologies, these systems show promise in overcoming the sensitivity barriers associated with rare mutation detection and protein quantification, enabling multi-omics data fusion. We also discuss how artificial intelligence (AI)-driven feature selection, clustering, and prediction integrate multidimensional data to decode tumor heterogeneity and guide disease monitoring. Despite rapid progress, key challenges remain-including the lack of standardization, limited integration of multi-omic datasets, and the need for robust clinical validation. Future directions may lie in the convergence of microfluidic-integrated materials, single-cell multi-omics, and AI-driven analytics to establish dynamic, high-resolution monitoring platforms that bridge the gap between fundamental research and clinical precision oncology.

title: Lipid-Based Nanotherapeutics for Inflammatory Disorders: Current Progress and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Aberrant inflammatory responses are crucial indicators of the onset and progression of diverse pathologies, including metabolic syndromes, autoimmune disorders, and neuroinflammation. The intrinsic intricacy and heterogeneity of these signaling pathways require innovative therapeutic approaches that allow precise immunomodulation while alleviating systemic toxicity. Lipid-based nanocarriers (LBNCs), including liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, and nanostructured lipid carriers, have emerged as transformative platforms to deliver a variety of therapeutic agents. The clinical maturity of these systems, catalyzed by the global success of lipid-based RNA vaccines, has established an initial safety and scalability of this framework, which is now being transitioned toward chronic inflammatory management. This review critically evaluates the structure-function relationships of LBNCs, examining how specific physicochemical attributes dictate their interaction with inflamed tissues. We analyze the molecular mechanisms by which LBNCs' architecture modulates key inflammatory regulators, such as cytokine networks and oxidative pathways, to achieve superior therapeutic control. Furthermore, we scrutinize the strategic selection of delivery routes and their direct impact on site-specific biodistribution and patient compliance. By addressing current bottlenecks in long-term immunocompatibility and regulatory characterization, this review provides a roadmap for engineering the next generation of bio-responsive anti-inflammatory nanomedicines. Collectively, these insights position LBNCs as a transformative paradigm for refining the precision and efficacy of modern anti-inflammatory therapy. This article is categorized under: Biology-Inspired Nanomaterials > Lipid-Based Structures.

title: Quantitative analysis of proteostasis disruption following siRNA-mediated HSP70 depletion in HeLa cells.
abstract: Heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) is a central molecular chaperone that maintains proteostasis by supporting protein folding, preventing protein aggregation, and coordinating cellular stress responses. Dysregulation of HSP70 has been associated with cancer progression, neurodegenerative disorders, and aging-related proteotoxicity. However, many experimental approaches rely on chemical inhibition or stress-inducing conditions that may introduce additional confounding effects. This study aimed to investigate the proteostatic consequences of HSP70 depletion in the absence of stress-inducing chemical inhibitors. A rapid, quantitative workflow was developed to assess chaperone function and proteostasis in cultured cells. HSP70 was depleted in HeLa cells using siRNA-mediated gene silencing. Knockdown efficiency was evaluated at the transcript and protein levels using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and Western blotting, respectively. Flow cytometry was used to quantify ProteoStat-detected misfolded/aggregated protein burden and total cellular fluorescence from a G3BP1-GFP reporter. siRNA-mediated HSP70 depletion resulted in a greater than 90% reduction in HSP70 transcript and protein levels. HSP70-depleted cells exhibited a 1.8-fold increase in ProteoStat fluorescence, indicating an increased burden of misfolded/aggregated proteins, and a 2.9-fold increase in total cellular G3BP1-GFP fluorescence. Because flow cytometry does not resolve intracellular localization or puncta formation, the increased G3BP1-GFP fluorescence should be interpreted as a surrogate reporter response and does not constitute direct evidence of stress granule biogenesis. These findings are consistent with impaired proteostasis following acute HSP70 depletion and demonstrate the potential utility of an inhibitor-independent workflow for evaluating cellular responses associated with targeted chaperone depletion. Orthogonal spatial validation using immunofluorescence or confocal microscopy is required to determine G3BP1 localization and confirm stress granule formation. In addition, experiments using multiple independent siRNA duplexes will be necessary to establish target specificity and strengthen the mechanistic interpretation of the observed proteostatic response.

title: Mogroside V Promotes Brown Adipose Thermogenesis via FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 Pathway to Combat Obesity.
abstract: Obesity is a chronic, recurrent, and progressive disease caused by energy imbalance. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification regulates fat thermogenesis, potentially counteracting obesity. Mogroside V (MV) is a triterpene glycoside extracted from Siraitia grosvenorii and has shown beneficial effects in models of obesity. However, its underlying mechanism remains unknown. The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of MV on adipose thermogenesis and explore the mechanism of m6A modifications in mediating these effects. Mitochondrial respiration analysis, histological and molecular biological methods were used to investigate the thermogenesis in differentiated C3H10T1/2 brown adipocytes and adipose tissue in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mouse models, respectively. Stable cell models with overexpression or knockdown of fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) were generated to investigate the effects of FTO on m6A modification and thermogenesis in brown adipocytes. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation-quantitative-PCR (MeRIP-qPCR) and RIP-qPCR analysis were used to reveal the potential downstream molecular targets of FTO. MV improved HFD-induced obesity and metabolic dysfunction in mice. MV also increased uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression in brown adipose tissue and enhanced mitochondrial respiration and expression of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ coactivator 1α (PGC1α) and UCP1 in differentiated C3H10T1/2 cells. Further analysis of the relevant molecular mechanisms showed that MV suppressed FTO expression, thereby increasing m6A modification of LETM1 domain-containing protein 1 (Letmd1) mRNA. The m6A-modified Letmd1 transcript was recognized by the m6A reader YTH domain-containing protein 2 (YTHDC2), thereby increasing the stability of Letmd1 mRNA. The increased Letmd1 mRNA levels were correlated with increased LETMD1 protein abundance, which subsequently enhanced the expression of PGC1α and UCP1, ultimately promoting brown adipocyte thermogenesis. MV promoted brown adipocyte thermogenesis through the FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 axis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity.

title: The nuclear oncoprotein SET is necessary for MLL/KMT2A mediated transcriptional activation.
abstract: The nuclear oncoprotein SET (patient "SE" translocation) has been implicated in the etiology of MLL (KMT2A) induced leukemia. Here we examine the details of this dependency in murine, primary hematopoietic cells. ChIP, RNAseq and immunoprecipitations demonstrated Set as downstream target of HoxA9 and confirmed a direct interaction with Mll. Set and Mll globally co-localized to promoter regions. Impairing Set expression phenocopied a knockdown of select Mll fusion targets with Set driving a pro-proliferative gene expression program that contained features indicative for Mll involvement. Molecularly, Set depletion caused dissociation of Mll from chromatin accompanied by a selective loss of RNA PolymeraseII Ser2-P. Concomitant with a function of Set as inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), specific recruitment of PP2A to the Meis1 promoter, a known Mll target, inhibited transcription in reporter assays and in the natural chromatin environment. We identified Mitogen and stress induced kinase 1 (Msk1) as potential substrate protected by Set from dephosphorylation. Phosphorylated Msk1-P colocalized with Mll and disappeared from chromatin upon Set depletion. Biochemically, Msk-1 bound directly to Mll as well as to menin, a known Mll tethering factor. Loss of Set/Mll/Msk1 selectively affected H3K14 acetylation at promoters and this could be partially attributed to the reduced presence of the histone acetyltransferase Moz (Kat6a). Finally, we show that kinase inhibitors augment menin inhibitor activity in MLL leukemia cells, indicating a connection between cellular signaling and MLL-function.

title: Sparse neuronal C4 elevation induces network-wide transcriptomic and lipid-droplet remodeling in the cortical microenvironment.
abstract: The complement component C4 regulates synaptic refinement and plasticity in the brain and has been implicated in multiple neurological and psychiatric disorders, with especially strong genetic evidence linking elevated C4A expression to schizophrenia. However, it remains unclear whether localized C4 elevation in a small neuronal population is sufficient to reshape broader cortical gene-regulatory programs and cellular phenotypes. To address this question, we overexpressed mouse C4 in approximately 2% of prefrontal cortical neurons using in utero electroporation and performed bulk RNA sequencing on microdissected prefrontal cortex. Despite the sparse manipulation, C4-OE was associated with broad transcriptional remodeling across tissue composed predominantly of untransfected cells, including coordinated changes in cholesterol biosynthesis, axon- and synaptic-associated programs, vascular/ECM pathways, and immune- and stress-related responses. Comparison with a schizophrenia synaptic proteomic dataset identified limited global correspondence but selective gene- and pathway-level overlap in specific molecular programs. Reference-based projection of directional DEG signatures onto a cortical single-cell transcriptomic reference further identified cell-type-associated structure, including prominent astrocyte- and vascular-associated axes and distinct lipid/metabolic, vascular/endothelial-interferon-associated, and immune/stress correlation domains. Spatial validation with MFISH showed increased Hmgcr expression in neighboring GFP-negative cells, while PLIN2 imaging revealed increased DAPI-associated/perinuclear lipid-droplet burden within the local C4-OE field. Together, these findings support a model in which sparse neuronal C4 elevation is associated with broader remodeling of the local cortical environment, including a non-cell-autonomous component involving neighboring-cell lipid-associated responses. These results expand the interpretation of C4 risk biology beyond synapse elimination alone and suggest that focal immune-gene dysregulation can engage lipid-homeostatic, stress-related, and cell-type-associated transcriptional programs relevant to cortical circuit vulnerability.

title: Alternative splicing acts as a strategic switch for heat shock network diversification under escalating heat stress.
abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) is a pivotal post-transcriptional mechanism for plant thermal adaptation, yet its dynamics in heat-tolerant woody species remain poorly understood. Here, we map the temperature-resolved AS landscape of the highly thermotolerant woody plant Rhododendron hainanense by combining Iso-Seq with RNA-seq. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a graded regulatory architecture: moderate heat (37 °C) elicited a targeted proteostatic response, whereas severe heat (42 °C) provoked a massive transcriptome expansion. Notably, this global AS surge coincided with a widespread downregulation of core splicing factors, a correlation suggesting that a more permissive splicing environment may contribute to the rapid generation of diverse stress-responsive isoforms. The heat shock protein (HSP) family emerged as the principal hub of this AS-associated diversification; the core chaperone genes ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70 generated the greatest transcript complexity, with HSP83 alone producing 29 distinct AS transcripts that resolved into three temperature-dependent expression groups. Within the heat shock factor network, HSFA2 showed the strongest and most sustained induction, and DAP-seq identified in vitro HSFA2 binding at the promoters of ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70, supporting these core chaperones as putative direct DNA-binding targets. Functional complementation in Arabidopsis further showed that three structurally distinct HSFA2 splice variants each restored thermotolerance to the hsfa2 mutant and consistently induced expression of the core ATP-dependent chaperone arm, suggesting that this central chaperone-induction capacity is retained across the tested splice variants in this heterologous system. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive atlas of temperature-modulated AS in a thermotolerant woody plant and support a model in which splicing-mediated diversification of the HSP chaperone network contributes to heat adaptation, offering post-transcriptional insights for breeding climate-resilient crops.

title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals the immune response mechanisms of Acrossocheilus fasciatus against Citrobacter freundii infection.
abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. In this study, we performed histological observation and RNA-seq analysis of the intestines and spleens of control (CK) and C. freundii infected A. fasciatus (EG). The results showed that infected fish exhibited abdominal haemorrhage, intestinal villous shedding, hydropic degeneration of hepatocytes and splenic sinus dilation with congestion. RNA-seq analysis identified 3054 DEGs in the intestine and 7706 DEGs in the spleen, with 1247 overlapping DEGs identified by combined analysis. A substantial portion of these genes clustered within biological activities linked to immunity and metabolic regulation, particularly engaging immune-related routes such as endoplasmic reticulum-based protein maturation, alongside the complement system and coagulation signalling cascades. This study systematically reveals the synergy and division of labor between the intestine and spleen during C. freundii infection, providing fundamental data for understanding the immune response mechanisms of A. fasciatus and a theoretical basis for optimising disease prevention and control strategies.

title: Lambda-cyhalothrin disrupts ion homeostasis and triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress in first-instar Tachypleus tridentatus: An integrated physiological-transcriptomic analysis.
abstract: Residual contamination of the type II pyrethroid lambda-cyhalothrin (LCT) is documented in coastal environments, posing potential risks to benthic fauna such as Tachypleus tridentatus. We integrated acute toxicity bioassays, histopathology, Na+/K+-ATPase and Ca2+-ATPase activity assays, and transcriptomic profiling to evaluate LCT-induced effects and mechanisms in first-instar larvae. The 48-h LC50 was 41.99 μg/L. Exposed larvae displayed characteristic neurotoxicity, including motor inhibition and sustained contraction of limbs and gills. Enzyme assays showed rapid and persistent suppression of Na+/K+-ATPase and a biphasic Ca2+-ATPase response (early elevation followed by suppression), consistent with disruption of Na+-Ca2+ exchange-coupled homeostasis. RNA-seq identified 975 differentially expressed genes enriched in endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress/unfolded protein response (UPR), redox regulation, immunity, and signaling pathways (e.g., Wnt, FoxO). Expression patterns (downregulation of BiP, HSP40, HSP90; upregulation of HSP70 isoforms, Jun-like factors, and phospholipase A2 isoforms) are consistent with ER dysfunction and secondary oxidative and immune stress. Collectively, these findings elucidate a toxicological cascade wherein LCT-induced VGSC perturbation precipitates ionoregulatory failure and subsequent ER stress/UPR activation, driving neuromuscular collapse. Beyond establishing toxicity benchmarks, the identified ATPase inhibition patterns and ER stress signatures provide specific mechanistic biomarkers for ecological risk assessment of pyrethroid exposure in benthic environments.

title: Cell cycle exit is required for differentiation and cell fate diversification but not neoblast specialisation in planarians
abstract: In planarians, adult stem cells constantly proliferate and differentiate into dozens of different cell types to maintain tissue homeostasis. However, how cell fate acquisition is coordinated with cell cycle progression remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from cells enriched for 2C or 4C DNA content and from animals subjected to RNAi against the cell cycle regulators cdh1 and h2b. We found that progenitor populations from multiple lineages contain actively cycling cells enriched in the 4C state. Cell fate acquisition to most cell types is acquired progressively during neoblast differentiation. Comparative analysis of cell cycle regulators confirmed a simplified regulatory repertoire in Schmidtea, supporting a central role for cdh1 in controlling cell cycle exit. RNAi-mediated knockdown of cdh1 caused homeostasis defects, impaired regeneration, accumulation of neoblasts and depletion of progenitors. Together, our findings demonstrate that cell cycle exit is required for terminal differentiation but not for neoblast specialisation. Instead, lineage commitment is initiated in actively cycling neoblasts, whereas terminal differentiation depends on cdh1-mediated cell cycle exit.

title: Suppressor with morphogenetic effect on genitalia 7 (SMG7) drives hepatocellular carcinoma progression through context-dependent nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) dysregulation.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the molecular mechanisms linking metabolic stress to tumor progression remain poorly defined. RNA surveillance pathways, including nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), may represent a relevant but unexplored regulatory layer in this context. In this study, we analyzed the expression of NMD components across multiple human HCC and MASLD cohorts, identifying suppressor with morphogenetic effect on genitalia 7 (SMG7) as a key regulator of NMD associated with HCC progression. In vitro functional assays, NMD target expression, transcriptomic profiling, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were used to identify downstream pathways and mediators. More than 40% of NMD components were dysregulated in HCC. Among them, SMG7 was consistently upregulated across HCC and MASLD cohorts, induced by lipotoxic stress, and identified as a hub gene in HCC transcriptional networks. SMG7 overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and clonogenicity, whereas its silencing reduced tumor aggressiveness in a context-dependent manner inversely associated with UPF1 levels. Combined depletion of SMG7 and UPF1 suppressed aggressive traits in vitro and limited tumor growth in vivo. Transcriptomic and network analyses identified Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) as a downstream mediator of SMG7 dysregulation in SNU-387 HCC cells, a finding further supported by functional rescue experiments. These results identify the SMG7-ZBP1 axis as a metabolic stress-responsive pathway linking NMD dysfunction to liver tumor progression and highlight NMD modulation as a therapeutic strategy to restrain tumor aggressiveness while enhancing tumor immunogenicity.

title: Age-related tumor mutational burden and inflammaging: a pan-cancer multi-omics study of treatment-naïve patients.
abstract: Aging is a major nonmodifiable risk factor for cancer, yet age-associated genomic instability, inflammatory activation, and tumor microenvironment interactions remain poorly characterized. The primary genomic cohort comprised 153 treatment-naïve patients with six cancer types, stratified at age 60 years; four additional patients without genomic profiling contributed to nongenomic analyses. Tumor mutational burden (TMB) and fraction genome altered were derived from whole-genome sequencing, and inflammatory pathway activity was determined from single-sample gene set enrichment analysis of RNA sequencing and proteomics in paired tumor and normal tissue. Because cancer type distribution differed between age groups, all principal associations were re-examined in multivariable models. TMB was higher in older patients (median 4.55 compared with 2.84 mutations per megabase; P < 0.001) and correlated with age (r s = 0.334, P < 0.001) but was attenuated by adjustment for cancer type and lost significance once microsatellite instability (MSI) status, sex, and stage were added (P = 0.27). Normal-tissue inflammation correlated with paired tumor TMB (protein r s =0.387, P < 0.001) but not after adjustment for age and cancer type (partial r s = 0.07, P = 0.54). MSI-high tumors showed greater tumor-normal inflammation amplification than non-MSI-high tumors (+0.065, P = 0.015), strengthening after adjustment (+0.087, P < 0.001). An immune-hot cluster arose only in older patients but was not independently associated with age (odds ratio 1.03, P = 0.61). Most age-associated molecular differences were substantially explained by cancer type. Only the age-related increase in normal-tissue inflammation at the protein level and the greater inflammation amplification of MSI-H tumors persisted. The correlation between normal-tissue inflammation and tumor TMB is not evidence that systemic inflammaging drives genomic instability.

title: Increased METTL1 expression in B cell subsets correlates with disease activity and immunological features in SLE.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by aberrant B cell activation, excessive plasma cell differentiation, and pathogenic autoantibody production. Epitranscriptomic modifications have emerged as important regulators of immune cell function. Among these, N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification, catalyzed by methyltransferase-like 1 (METTL1), has been implicated in immune regulation and autoimmune diseases. However, the expression pattern of METTL1 across peripheral B cell subsets and its clinical relevance in SLE remain incompletely characterized. m7G levels and METTL1 expression were examined in mouse B cells and plasma cells using dot blot and RT-qPCR. METTL1 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and B cell subsets from patients with SLE and healthy controls was assessed by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between METTL1 expression and disease activity, clinical manifestations, autoantibodies, and laboratory parameters, with multiple testing controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. To explore molecular programs associated with METTL1, RNA sequencing was conducted in B cells isolated from wild-type and Mettl1-deficient mice, followed by Gene Ontology, gene set enrichment, protein-protein interaction, and motif analyses. m7G modification and METTL1 expression were significantly elevated in mouse plasma cells compared with B cells. In patients with SLE, METTL1 was markedly upregulated in PBMCs and across B cell subsets, with the highest expression observed in plasmablasts (PBs). Importantly, METTL1 expression was positively correlated with SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) scores in total B cells, NBs, MBs, and PBs, and all four associations remained significant after FDR correction. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that METTL1 deficiency was associated with downregulation of immune-related processes and proliferative pathways, including MYC targets, E2F targets, and G2M checkpoint signaling. METTL1 is highly expressed in B cells, particularly PBs, in SLE and is consistently associated with disease activity as measured by SLEDAI. Transcriptomic analyses further link METTL1 to key transcriptional programs involved in B cell function. These findings provide a subset-resolved characterization of METTL1 in SLE and support further investigation of its clinical and biological relevance in B cell dysregulation.

title: CD147+ Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promote PD-L1 Expression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 Signaling.
abstract: Targeting CD147 on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) have been identified as critical components of the tumor microenvironment. The role of CD147 in CAFs is still unclear, and this study aims to explore its function. We analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data to identify CD147 expression in CAFs. Flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) were used to validate protein levels. CD147 function was assessed via shRNA/overexpression. Protein interactions were examined by molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Organoid co-culture system was established to study tumor-immune interactions. Single-cell sequencing and mIHC analyses have confirmed the presence of CD147+CAFs within tumor and adjacent tissues, with tumor-derived CAFs exhibiting elevated CD147 transcript levels. The proportion of CD147+ CAFs varied among patients and demonstrated no significant correlation with CD147 expression in HCC cells. Functionally, CD147+ CAFs secreted higher levels of IL-6 compared to CD147- counterparts. We elucidated a mechanism wherein CD147 on CAFs competitively binds to the tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP2), thereby diminishing TIMP2-mediated inhibition of matrix metalloproteinase 2 (MMP2). Free MMP2 enhances IL-6 secretion via the integrin α5β1 signaling pathway. IL-6 subsequently upregulates PD-L1 expression on HCC cells. This phenomenon was validated both in vitro and organoid co-culture model, where a higher burden of CD147+ CAFs correlated with increased levels of IL-6 and PD-L1. Our study delineates a novel CAF-driven immunosuppressive pathway in HCC, where CD147+ CAFs enhance tumor cell PD-L1 expression and susceptibility to immune checkpoint blockade via a TIMP2/MMP2/IL-6 axis. CD147 has been primarily viewed as a therapeutic marker on HCC cells and has supported the development of CD147-targeted treatment strategies. This study shows that CD147 is also expressed in CAFs and functions as an independent regulator of the immune microenvironment by promoting IL 6 secretion and tumor PD-L1 upregulation. Importantly, CD147 expression in CAFs is not correlated with its expression in tumor cells. These findings suggest that evaluation of CD147 in both tumor and stromal compartments may improve patient stratification and may identify additional patients who could potentially benefit from CD147-targeted or combination immunotherapy approaches.

title: Prostate Cancer Patient-Derived Organoids (PDOs) as Functional Avatars for Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO)-Based Personalized Therapy.
abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDOs) closely preserve the cellular heterogeneity, histopathology, and molecular features of the original tumors, making them powerful preclinical models. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are an emerging class of precision medicines that modulate gene expression at the RNA level with high target specificity, yet their application in organoid systems remains underexplored. Here, we adapted previously described protocols to establish a biobank of prostate cancer (PC) PDOs, achieving a high initial growth success rate (>90%). Histological and molecular analyses confirmed the preservation of key tumor features. Using these models, we assessed several ASOs, with particular emphasis on OGX-427 (Apatorsen), an ASO targeting heat shock protein 27 (HSP27) that has been evaluated in phase I/II clinical trials. While OGX-427 effectively suppressed HSP27 expression and inhibited cell growth in 2D cultures, its efficacy was markedly limited in 3D organoids, likely due to extracellular matrix and structural barriers. Removing Matrigel and applying single-cell transfection overcame these barriers, achieving efficient ASO uptake, significant target protein downregulation, and robust, dose-dependent inhibition of organoid growth. These findings underscore the utility of PDOs for evaluating ASO-based therapies and their potential to accelerate precision oncology strategies for PC and other malignancies.

title: PLPP1 inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling via enhancing Caveolin-1/β-catenin interaction and is negatively regulated by c-Myc in osteosarcoma.
abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents, characterized by rapid progression and poor prognosis. The molecular mechanisms underlying OS malignancy remain incompletely understood. Phospholipid phosphatase 1 (PLPP1) has recently been implicated in cancer biology, yet its role in OS is largely unknown. RNA sequence data from TARGET-OS and GEO cohorts were downloaded and analyzed for assessing the relationship between PLPP1 expression levels and the OS prognosis. PLPP1 expression levels in OS cells and samples were detected using qRT-PCR, WB and immunohistochemistry. The effects of PLPP1 on proliferation, migration, invasion and chemosensitivity of OS cells were evaluated by up- or down-regulated PLLP1 expression. In vivo subcutaneous and tail-vein xenograft models were used to examine tumor growth and metastasis. Then, transcriptome profiling, luciferase reporter assays, co-immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence and ChIP-PCR were conducted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms. PLPP1 was markedly down-regulated in OS tissues and cell lines. And low expression level of PLPP1 was correlated with poor prognosis, advanced clinical stage and metastasis. Functionally, PLPP1 overexpression inhibited OS cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and enhanced chemotherapy-induced apoptosis; conversely, silencing PLPP1 produced the opposite effects. In vivo, PLPP1 overexpression suppressed tumor growth and lung metastasis. Mechanistically, overexpression of PLPP1 impaired strength of Wnt/β-catenin signaling without altering β-catenin abundance, but instead inhibited β-catenin nuclear import by enhancing Caveolin-1/β-catenin interaction. Furthermore, PLPP1 was transcriptionally repressed by c-Myc, which directly bound to the PLPP1 promoter. Rescue experiments confirmed that c-Myc promoted OS malignancy by repressing PLPP1, thereby activating Wnt/β-catenin signaling. This study identified PLPP1 as a prognostic suppressor in OS that inhibited β-catenin nuclear import through enhancing Caveolin-1/β-catenin interaction and was transcriptionally repressed by c-Myc. Targeting the c-Myc/PLPP1/β-catenin axis might represent a promising therapeutic strategy for OS. This study revealed the potential of PLPP1 as a novel prognostic biomarker of OS, and suggested its potential for therapeutic applications by specifically activating PLPP1 expression using small-molecule activators.

title: Integrative bioinformatics screening of a M2 macrophage-associated gene signature for osimertinib resistance.
abstract: Although the third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) Osimertinib is widely used in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), acquired resistance to this agent remains a major clinical challenge perplexing the academic community. While the genomic drivers of osimertinib resistance (OR) have been relatively well characterized, the non-genetic contributions of the tumor microenvironment (TME), especially the role of macrophage-mediated remodeling remains incompletely understood. To address this gap, a total of 6 lung cancer tissue samples were collected from a cohort of 6 NSCLC patients and subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed on Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) data to screen out OR-associated gene modules. The intersection of scRNA-seq-derived differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and module genes was used to identify M2 macrophage- and OR-related DEGs (MORGs). An ensemble machine learning framework encompassing 112 algorithm combinations was applied to construct a gene signature. Survival analysis was conducted in the EGFR-mutant TCGA cohort. In vitro cell experiments were further performed for functional validation. Single-cell RNA sequencing firstly revealed an increased proportion of M2 macrophages in the OR group, and M2 macrophage-specific DEGs were identified between OR and non-OR groups. A total of seven MORGs were obtained by intersecting DEGs and OR-related module genes. A 7-gene signature was successfully established via machine learning. Survival analysis demonstrated that RRBP1 showed the strongest association with overall survival and was selected for further investigation. In vitro experiments confirmed that RRBP1 was significantly upregulated in the H1975OR cells. Knockdown of RRBP1 reduced cell viability and migration, lowered the IC50 of osimertinib, and increased the expression of ER stress markers such as GRP78 and CHOP. In summary, our study identified a 7-MORGs signature for OR, among which RRBP1 may be a candidate regulator for OR.

title: Single-Cell Multiomics Reveals That OTUD7B Is a Central Driver of Epithelial Remodelling and the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extreme malignancy and profound resistance to therapy, largely driven by a fibrotic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME). The deubiquitinase OTU domain-containing protein 7B (OTUD7B) has been implicated in inflammatory and oncogenic signalling, but its role in PAAD and its TME remains unclear. This study integrated single-cell RNA-seq datasets from the GEO and bulk RNA-seq data from the TCGA to delineate the cellular ecosystem of PAAD, and employed cell-cell communication analysis, high-dimensional weighted gene coexpression network analysis (hdWGCNA), and nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) to identify OTUD7B-associated modules and epithelial subpopulations, while assessing the survival and clinicopathologic correlations of OTUD7B in the TCGA-PAAD cohort. Quantitative proteomics of OTUD7B-knockout PAAD cells was performed and combined with GO/KEGG and GSEA to explore downstream pathways, and immune infiltration was inferred by deconvolution algorithms and validated by multiplex immunofluorescence staining of OTUD7B, CD4, and FOXP3. Single-cell RNA-seq revealed the expansion of epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages with dense ligand-receptor networks, alongside the depletion of effector T and NK cells, indicating a shift toward an immunosuppressive TME. hdWGCNA identified epithelial-ECM modules in which OTUD7B served as a hub gene, and NMF revealed an OTUD7B-high epithelial subset enriched in glycosylation-related metabolic programs and positioned at an early stage of the malignant trajectory. OTUD7B was significantly upregulated in PAAD and was associated with higher grade, lymph node metastasis, and advanced stage, and predicted poorer overall survival. Proteomic profiling of OTUD7B-deficient cells revealed broad remodelling of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, ROS metabolism, and redox homeostasis. OTUD7B expression was positively correlated with M2 macrophage infiltration, immunomodulatory gene expression, and CD4+FOXP3+ regulatory T-cell accumulation, and tissue staining further confirmed the positive association between OTUD7B expression and Treg-rich regions. Collectively, OTUD7B acts as a key integrative node that links epithelial remodelling, mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming, and TME immunosuppression in PAAD, serving as an adverse prognostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target to remodel tumour metabolism and enhance antitumor immunity.
